title: Production verifier authority provider for the agent wrapper
description:
PREREQUISITE of task-97554aa4293e40eab56c0b642e18513a (Foundation self-host canary), discovered at the canary's step-1 resume-gate re-measurement on 2026-08-17.

MEASURED GAP at committed HEAD a42ae2f1f9168d13b8b786404fc47b366cc8edd9 (git grep against HEAD, not the working tree):

  git grep -n "verificationAuthority" HEAD -- apps/ packages/ | grep -v '\.test\.'
    apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts:240:      verificationAuthority: () => null,
    apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.ts:62:  readonly verificationAuthority: (
    apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.ts:165:      const authority = config.verificationAuthority(nodeRef, brief);

  git grep -n "VerifierAuthorityFacts" HEAD -- apps/ packages/ | grep -v '\.test\.'
    -> only the type declaration (review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:15), its re-export
       (review/verifier-receipt-ledger.ts:22) and two consuming positions. ZERO producers.

THE DEFECT. The only production host that constructs the node verifier -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts, the real `agent-wrapper-main.js` entry the canary must spawn -- passes `verificationAuthority: () => null`, with the shipped comment "No production authority provider is shipped yet. Refuse a green test rather than manufacture calibration, package or policy facts in-process."

node-verifier.ts:165-172 turns that null into, for EVERY node:
    reports.push({ detail: "host verifier authority unavailable", nodeRef,
                   outcome: "VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE" });
    continue;

So `recordVerifierReceipt` (node-verifier.ts:176) is unreachable and the `integration.accept_output` dispatch (node-verifier.ts:152, :198) never fires through the production host. The refusal is honest and correctly fails closed -- this task is NOT a request to weaken it. It is the missing producer.

WHY IT BLOCKS THE CANARY. Canary DoD 3 requires one exclusive task to complete "plan, execute, verify, independent review, accept ... with exact receipts", and canary plan step 3 requires the journey to "execute the real verifier, independent review and final acceptance" through production surfaces. With no authority producer, the only reachable verify outcome is VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE. Global rail Clause 2 forbids the alternatives: no narrowed DoD, no mock-backed journey, no authority reimplemented inside the E2E test.

Objective: ship the daemon-owned producer of `VerifierAuthorityFacts` and wire it into agent-wrapper-main, so a node with genuine durable calibration/package/policy facts verifies and earns a receipt, while a node WITHOUT them still refuses with the same stable outcome.

Deliverable: a focused daemon module (suggested apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.ts plus its one-line .js bridge) that reads the facts from the durable store -- never from caller input, never minted in-process -- plus focused tests; and the agent-wrapper-main.ts:240 edit replacing `() => null` with that provider.

NOT in scope: changing the VerifierAuthorityFacts shape, the receipt ledger, review-services acceptance, or anything under tests/e2e/foundation.

Read verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:15 for the exact required fields BEFORE planning, and confirm each field has a durable source; if any field has no durable source on disk, that is a further prerequisite to file, not a field to fabricate.
definitionOfDone: A production daemon module produces VerifierAuthorityFacts by reading the durable store; git grep shows it is the value passed at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts, and `verificationAuthority: () => null` no longer appears anywhere in production.

Every field of VerifierAuthorityFacts (per apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:15) is sourced from a durable record; a test proves no field is defaulted, minted in-process, or read from caller input.

A test drives the real createNodeVerifier with the real provider over a seeded store and asserts a receipt was recorded via recordVerifierReceipt and the integration.accept_output dispatch fired -- asserting the receipt identity, not merely ok:true.
A test with the durable facts ABSENT asserts the literal outcome string VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE and that no receipt row was written; the fail-closed path is preserved, not weakened.
A mutation drill on the provider's durable read makes the receipt-recording test go red for its receipt assertion (not for a crash), and production bytes are restored exactly.
pnpm typecheck and pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test are exit 0 with a nonzero printed Test Files count line; owned production files are each <=250 physical lines.
taskRails: Fail closed with stable reason codes; an absent durable fact stays VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE and never gains authority by default.
Do not weaken or delete the existing refusal branch at node-verifier.ts:165-172; add the producer, keep the guard.
Use TDD. Keep each production source focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Stage and commit only explicit owned paths by pathspec; no git add -A, no worktree, no push, no merge.

implementationPlan.description: Re-measure on committed HEAD, then RESOLVE THE PER-FIELD AUTHORITY MATRIX before writing any production line. `VerifierAuthorityFacts` (apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:15) has exactly three fields: `calibration: ReviewerCalibration`, `packageItems: readonly ReviewPackageItemInput[]`, `policy: PolicyEvaluationInput`. Confirm with `git grep -n "verificationAuthority\|VerifierAuthorityFacts" HEAD -- apps/ packages/ | grep -v '\.test\.'` that agent-wrapper-main.ts still passes `() => null` and that ZERO producers exist; if a producer has landed meanwhile, STOP and report the task already closed rather than adding a second one. Then write down, in the step note, the durable source for each field. Architect's measurement at HEAD a42ae2f, to be re-confirmed not re-derived: (a) POLICY has a durable source -- `installPolicy` (bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-services.ts:42) commits a `PolicyInstalled` event and folds `{slices: {[sliceRef]: slice}}`, readable via the `installedSlices`/`stateOf` shape on the bootstrap ledger aggregate; (b) PACKAGE ITEMS are `{digest, kind, locator}` over the frozen `REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEM_KINDS` allow-list and are derivable from durable review state -- `readReviewLedger(store, projectId, nodeRef)` already yields `latest.resultSha256`, `latest.decisionId` and `aggregateVersion` at node-verifier.ts:137-144; (c) CALIBRATION is `{corpusRevision, sentinelPassed, staleness}` and its own contract comment (packages/review/src/review-contract.ts:127) says "Both are caller-supplied durable facts" -- there is NO durable producer on disk today. Decide and record ONE lawful durable home for calibration; the installed-policy slice keyed by an explicit sliceRef is the intended candidate because it is an existing durable mechanism that requires a real prior `policy.install` command. If you cannot bind calibration to a durable record that a real command writes, call `moe.report_blocked` naming the field and the absent writer -- do NOT default it, mint it in-process, or read it from `NodeMission`.

RED. Add apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.test.ts against a real `SqliteEventStore` (open a temp-file store; do not stub it). Write the failing tests for the provider's contract BEFORE the module exists: (1) with every durable record seeded, `createVerifierAuthorityProvider({store, projectId})(nodeRef, brief)` returns a frozen `VerifierAuthorityFacts` whose policy fields equal the INSTALLED slice bytes, whose packageItems digests equal the durable review digests, and whose calibration equals the durably recorded calibration -- assert the exact values, never `toBeTruthy`; (2) with the policy slice absent it returns `null`; (3) with the calibration record absent it returns `null`; (4) with the review ledger unreadable or holding no accepted-route round it returns `null`. Every negative case must ALSO assert that the store's raw event count is unchanged, so a provider that writes on a read path fails. Per the epic rail on reason codes: because `null` is this port's single refusal channel, each negative test must additionally assert WHICH durable record was missing by seeding exactly one gap at a time and asserting the other three positive cases still pass in the same test file -- a single `expect(result).toBeNull()` with all records absent is the vacuous shape this rail forbids.

GREEN. Create apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./verifier-authority-provider.ts";` -- required, a new .ts module without it is invisible to the .js import graph). Export `createVerifierAuthorityProvider(config: {store: SqliteEventStore; projectId: string}): (nodeRef: string, brief: NodeMission) => VerifierAuthorityFacts | null`, matching `NodeVerifierConfig.verificationAuthority` at node-verifier.ts:62-65 EXACTLY so no call-site type change is needed. It reads the installed policy slice from the bootstrap ledger aggregate, the calibration from the durable home fixed in step 1, and derives packageItems from `readReviewLedger`; every returned object is `Object.freeze`d. Any read that throws, any absent record, any digest failing the receipt contract's HEX64 shape, and any item kind outside `REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEM_KINDS` returns `null` -- never a partial fact set and never a default. The provider performs NO writes. Keep the file <=250 physical lines; if the three readers push it past that, split the readers into a sibling module rather than trimming validation.

RED then GREEN on the real verifier composition, in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.test.ts (extend it; do not create a parallel suite). Drive the REAL `createNodeVerifier` with the REAL provider from step 3 over a seeded store -- no stub authority function anywhere in these two cases. Case A (earns a receipt): seed the durable policy slice, calibration, and a review ledger whose latest round routes ACCEPT, supply a `runTest` returning `exitCode: 0` with a known output sha, and assert (i) the report outcome is exactly `"ACCEPTED"`, (ii) `readVerifierReceipt(store, projectId, verifierReceiptId(projectId, nodeRef, latest.decisionId))` returns `ok: true`, (iii) the stored receipt's `execution.outputSha256` equals the capture sha and its `calibration`/`policy`/`packageItems` are byte-equal to the provider's return -- assert the receipt IDENTITY and contents, not `ok: true` alone. Case B (fail-closed preserved): identical seeding minus the calibration record, and assert the report outcome is the literal string `"VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE"`, that `runTest` was never invoked (the authority check at node-verifier.ts:165 precedes the run at :173), and that no receipt row exists.

Wire the production host. Replace `verificationAuthority: () => null,` at apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts:240 with the step-3 provider constructed from the wrapper's already-open `verifierStore` and `config.projectId` (both are in scope at that point -- `verifierStore = SqliteEventStore.open(config.storePath)` is assigned immediately above the `createNodeVerifier` call). Delete the now-false comment on the preceding lines ("No production authority provider is shipped yet...") and replace it with one line stating that absent durable facts still yield VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE. Change nothing else in this file: the spawner, MCP host, verifier runner and stop plumbing are out of scope. Then prove the wiring by grep, not by reading: `git grep -n "verificationAuthority" -- apps/ | grep -v '\.test\.'` must show the provider at the wrapper call site and must NOT show `() => null` anywhere in production.

Mutation drills, two of them, because "wiring exists" and "wiring fails closed" are separate claims. Drill 1 (composition): in verifier-authority-provider.ts make the durable calibration read return a hard-coded literal instead of the stored value; the step-4 Case A receipt-content assertion must go RED on the calibration comparison -- if it goes red on a crash or a different assertion, the test is not pinning the durable read and must be strengthened. Drill 2 (fail-closed): make the absent-record branch return a fabricated facts object instead of `null`; the step-4 Case B assertion on the literal `"VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE"` must go RED. Record for each drill the exact command, the failing test NAME, and the assertion that failed. Restore exact bytes after each drill and verify with `git diff --numstat -- apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.ts` showing 0 added and 0 deleted lines; the shared worktree makes `git checkout` a hazard, so restore by re-editing, not by checkout. Run the drills one at a time -- a peer commit landing mid-drill can otherwise swallow the patch and leave git reading clean.

Adversarial self-review, then commit by explicit pathspec. Read the whole owned diff as an attacker: can any field of the returned facts originate from `NodeMission`, from a command payload, or from a default? Does any negative path still permit a receipt? Does the provider write, or hold, a store handle that outlives the verifier (a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker)? Is the frozen `REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEM_KINDS` allow-list honoured, and does an item kind outside it refuse rather than pass through? Is the failure-round path at node-verifier.ts:88-98 -- which still uses the synthetic `PACKAGE_ITEM_FILL` digests -- left untouched, as it must be? Confirm no production file exceeds 250 physical lines. Then `git status --porcelain`, unstage any foreign entry with `git restore --staged -- <path>`, and commit ONLY these five paths by explicit pathspec: apps/daemon/src/review/verifier-authority-provider.ts, .js, .test.ts, apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/node-verifier.test.ts, apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts. Verify with `git show --stat` that no foreign path is present. If a foreign whole-tree completion already captured these bytes, do NOT amend or reset -- record the merge-base diff for QA instead.

Verification gate. Run in the FOREGROUND, chained with `&&` so a red leg cannot be masked (a `;` chain reports only the last command; a pipe reports the tail's exit code): `pnpm typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: `pnpm --filter <pkg>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 when the package name does not resolve, so the leg is only evidence if it prints a `Test Files N passed` count line with N nonzero -- `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon, and a run with no count line is UNVERIFIED, not passing. Confirm the two new test names from steps 2 and 4 appear in the run. Repo-wide red is compared against the merge-base baseline and may be disclosed only when the new failing-path delta intersected with this task's five owned paths is empty; a red inside the owned paths is a block, not a disclosure. This command's fresh output is the sole `complete_task` verification evidence.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected: (a) letting the wrapper mint calibration/policy in-process -- that is exactly what the shipped comment refuses and what epic rail 4 forbids; (b) widening NodeVerifierConfig or changing VerifierAuthorityFacts -- the port shape is already correct, only its producer is missing; (c) reading the facts from NodeMission (the node spec JSON on disk) -- spec files are host-owned input, not durable authority, and a spec file is writable by any agent in the shared tree; (d) filing a further prerequisite for calibration -- policy.install already provides a durable, command-written, sliceRef-keyed home, so a new durable writer would be a duplicate mechanism. Step 1 keeps the escape hatch: if the worker cannot bind calibration to a record a real command writes, it blocks rather than defaults. Chose a single focused provider module over three per-field modules because the three reads share one refusal channel (null) and splitting them would spread the fail-closed decision across files.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at committed HEAD a42ae2f with `git grep <sym> HEAD` (the working tree is foreign-dirty and must not be trusted). VerifierAuthorityFacts is declared at review/verifier-receipt-contracts.ts:15 with exactly three fields and is re-exported from review/verifier-receipt-ledger.ts:22 -- import the TYPE from the ledger path, which is what node-verifier.ts:16 already does. The port is NodeVerifierConfig.verificationAuthority at node-verifier.ts:62-65, called at :165; on null it pushes outcome VERIFICATION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE and `continue`s at :166-173, so recordVerifierReceipt (:176) and the integration.accept_output dispatch (:152 replay path, :198 fresh path) are unreachable today. The single production construction site is agent-wrapper-main.ts:240, inside the same block that opens `verifierStore` and holds `config.projectId` -- no new plumbing is needed to reach a store. Durable sources: policy is folded by installPolicy (bootstrap/bootstrap-policy-services.ts:42-61) as `{slices: {[sliceRef]: slice}}` behind a PolicyInstalled event, read via installedSlices/stateOf; review digests come from readReviewLedger (review/review-read-model.ts) which node-verifier already calls at :137 and whose `latest` carries resultSha256/decisionId/aggregateVersion; package item kinds are the frozen REVIEW_PACKAGE_ITEM_KINDS allow-list (CRITERION, DAEMON_ARTIFACT, DAEMON_RECEIPT, GRAPH_HASH, INTEGRATED_TREE, PLAN_HASH, RUBRIC, SUBMITTED_BYTES) at packages/review/src/review-contract.ts:150. ReviewerCalibration is {corpusRevision, sentinelPassed, staleness} at review-contract.ts:128 and has ZERO durable producers -- only review-test-fixtures.ts:249 mints one. A new .ts module in this repo needs a one-line .js bridge or it is invisible to the .js import graph.
planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is fabrication: two of the three fields have no durable writer today, and the cheapest wrong fix is a literal default that makes every node verify. Step 1 forces the per-field decision and permits report_blocked; steps 2 and 6 make a fabricated value fail a named test. Second risk is a vacuous negative suite -- `expect(result).toBeNull()` with everything absent passes even if the provider ignores the store entirely, which is why step 2 requires one seeded gap at a time plus a passing positive control in the same file. Third, do not touch the failure-round payload at node-verifier.ts:88-98: its PACKAGE_ITEM_FILL digests are synthetic by disclosed design and rewriting them is out of scope. Fourth, ordering: the authority check precedes runTest, so Case B must assert runTest was never called -- otherwise a reordering regression stays green. Fifth, SqliteEventStore handles must be closed on every path in tests; a held handle kills the vitest worker outright. Sixth, the shared worktree makes `git checkout` a destructive restore and makes a peer commit able to swallow a drill patch -- restore drills by re-editing and confirm with `git diff --numstat` showing zero added lines. Finally, this task is a hard prerequisite of the Foundation self-host canary (task-97554aa4, GAP E); its completion note should name that task as the consumer edge.

blockedReason:
Step-1 authority matrix re-measured at HEAD a42ae2f. Gap confirmed open (agent-wrapper-main.ts:240 still `() => null`; zero producers). BLOCKING: 2 of 3 VerifierAuthorityFacts fields have NO durable source, so the provider cannot be built without fabricating.

(1) policy — OK. installPolicy (bootstrap-policy-services.ts:42-61) folds {slices:{[sliceRef]:slice}} behind PolicyInstalled, readable via installedSlices/stateOf. policy.install allow-list is ["slice"] (daemon-command-registry.ts:113).

(2) calibration — NO DURABLE WRITER, as step 1 anticipated. ReviewerCalibration {corpusRevision,sentinelPassed,staleness} (review-contract.ts:128); only producer on disk is review-test-fixtures.ts:249.

(3) packageItems — NO DURABLE SOURCE. New, and contradicts step-1 premise (b): NOT derivable from readReviewLedger. ReviewRoundRecord (review-read-model.ts:21-30) carries only aggregateVersion/decisionId/lineage/principalId/reviewInputDigest/resultSha256/round/routing — no items. submitRound (review-services.ts:150-155) commits {lineage,reviewInputDigest,round,routing} and DISCARDS the payload items. Not recoverable from the request either: CommandDecisionRecordBase (store-contracts.ts:86-106) retains requestSha256 only, no requestBytes. buildReviewPackage needs >=1 CRITERION plus singleton GRAPH_HASH/PLAN_HASH/RUBRIC/SUBMITTED_BYTES/INTEGRATED_TREE (review-package.ts:119-134); recordVerifierReceipt refuses a provider DAEMON_RECEIPT (verifier-receipt-ledger.ts:178). Every production instance of those kinds is a synthetic literal: node-verifier.ts:93-97 PACKAGE_ITEM_FILL (disclosed-synthetic, out of scope) and live-dispatch.ts:144-148 hex64(). NodeMission is {instructions,test,title,workspace} (agent-wrapper.ts:47-52) and carries none.

Deriving 6 items with 64-hex digests from 3 scalars is minting. The task's own text ("no durable source = a prerequisite to file, not a field to fabricate"), Clause 2 and rail 4 require a prerequisite, not a narrowed DoD or in-test authority.

priorHandoffs.pitfalls: The decisive trap: 'derive packageItems from durable review state' reads plausible and measures false. submitRound (review-services.ts:150-155) commits only {lineage,reviewInputDigest,round,routing} and DISCARDS the payload items, and they are not recoverable from the request either — CommandDecisionRecordBase (store-contracts.ts:86-106) exposes resultBytes and requestSha256 but has NO requestBytes field. So the durable record holds a hash of the package, never its contents. Producing six 64-hex content digests from three scalars (resultSha256/decisionId/aggregateVersion) is minting, not deriving, and would yield a receipt whose reviewInputDigest is unbound from anything a reviewer saw. Do not source any field from NodeMission — it is {instructions,test,title,workspace} (agent-wrapper.ts:47-52) and carries none of the three fields; it is also host-owned input, not durable authority. Do not reuse the PACKAGE_ITEM_FILL synthetic set at node-verifier.ts:93-97: it is disclosed-synthetic and explicitly out of scope. Do not weaken the refusal at node-verifier.ts:165-173 — note it correctly precedes runTest at :174, so a fail-closed test asserting 'runTest never invoked' is sound. Nothing was edited: git status --porcelain over apps/daemon/src/review/ and apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/ was empty at HEAD a42ae2f, and there is no commit for this task.
priorHandoffs.openQuestions: (A) Where should the round's package items durably live? Natural fix is for submitRound to persist the admitted items in its committed result (or a sibling record keyed by decisionId) with review-read-model.ts parseRound surfacing them — but review-services is outside this task's stated scope, so it needs its own task. Worth noting GRAPH_HASH/PLAN_HASH have durable analogues on the graph_revision aggregate (graphContentHash/planHash) while RUBRIC/SUBMITTED_BYTES/INTEGRATED_TREE/CRITERION have no durable producer at all — and the daemon wires no graph.* kinds, the same Graph Beta gap that blocked task-a9fd91c3. (B) Is a policy.install slice keyed by an explicit sliceRef the sanctioned durable home for calibration? It looks lawful — the allow-list admits an arbitrary slice object and review-contract.ts:127 calls calibration 'caller-supplied durable facts', so caller-supplied-then-durably-written is the contract's own shape — but that is a design call for an architect, not a worker. I did not implement (B) alone because the provider must return all three fields or null, so without (A) there is no provider.
